title: Transit Gateway and peering
scenario: Mossgiel Outfitters runs 14 VPCs today, one per team, and expects 30 within 12 months. Every VPC must be able to reach every other VPC and the head-office network, which connects through a single VPN now and will gain a Direct Connect link next year. Two of the 14, the catalogue-data VPC and the analytics VPC, exchange about 80 TB a month with each other and with nothing else in volume. Network changes are made by a two-person team.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Adding a new VPC must not require editing or linking to each existing VPC
Finance wants the 80 TB a month between the catalogue-data and analytics VPCs kept off any per-gigabyte processing charge that the other VPCs' shared path incurs
The head-office VPN and the future Direct Connect link must reach all VPCs without per-VPC connections
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
All 14 VPCs, the head-office VPN and the later Direct Connect link are connected so that onboarding a 31st VPC needs connections from that VPC only, and no existing VPC's configuration is edited
The 80 TB a month between the catalogue-data and analytics VPCs avoids the per-gigabyte processing charge that the other VPCs' traffic incurs, and the record shows the basis

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
